citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \langle u,v\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,$$
with the second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]; the real momentum dot product and norm are those of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Explicitly extend the real dot product
complex-bilinearly to $a\cdot b=\sum_{j=1}^3a_jb_j$ for $a,b\in\mathbb C^3$.
Each complex fiber instead has the positive Hermitian pairing
$\langle a,b\rangle_2=\overline a\cdot b=\sum_j\overline a_jb_j$ and
norm $\|a\|^2=\sum_j|a_j|^2$; the displayed integral uses this pairing.
Hilbert completeness follows from [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For $\mathbf k\ne0$, write $n(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-n(\mathbf k)n(\mathbf k)^T.$$
Assign any value at $\mathbf k=0$, which is a Lebesgue-null set. Let $M_{P_T}$ be multiplication by this measurable matrix field and define the positive transverse photon space
$$\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T} =\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}.$$
The inner product on $\mathcal H_T$ is the restriction of that on $\mathcal H$. Each nonzero momentum fiber is the two-complex-dimensional plane $\{a\in\mathbb C^3:\mathbf k\cdot a=0\}$ perpendicular to the real vector $\mathbf k$ in that Hermitian pairing; no global continuous polarization frame is part of the definition.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and let $H$ be a separable
complex Hilbert space with the second-variable-linear convention of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ define the bosonic
creation and annihilation maps $a^\dagger(h)$ and $a(h)$ and the fermionic maps
$c^\dagger(h)$ and $c(h)$ as in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Write $a_n(h)$ and $a_n^\dagger(h)$ for
their restrictions to the $n$th bosonic sector. For bosons set

$$D(a(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge1}\|a_n(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\},\qquad D(a^\dagger(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge0}\|a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}.$$

Then $\mathcal F_s(H)$ and $\mathcal F_a(H)$ are Hilbert spaces,
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is dense, and it is a graph core for both maximal
bosonic sector maps. The bosonic operators on their displayed domains are
closed and mutually adjoint, and on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ satisfy

$$[a(h),a^\dagger(k)]=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad [a(h),a(k)]=[a^\dagger(h),a^\dagger(k)]=0.$$

The fermionic $c(h)$ and $c^\dagger(h)$ extend to bounded operators on the
whole Fock space, with norms $\|h\|$, and satisfy on the whole space

$$\{c(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad \{c(h),c(k)\}=\{c^\dagger(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=0.$$

This is a mathematical construction of the two Fock representations; it does
not assign particle statistics to a physical species.

For an integer $d\ge1$, let $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ be the complex Schwartz space with seminorms
$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$
for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$; this is exactly
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]. Let
$\mathcal D(\mathbb R^d)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with the support convention of
[[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]] and the locally convex LF topology of
[[def-test-function-topology]]. The tempered-distribution space $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^d)$
is the space of continuous complex-linear functionals on this topological
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, paired bilinearly with test functions, as in
[[def-tempered-distribution]].

For every complex Hilbert space $H$, use the second-variable-linear pairing
$\langle u,v\rangle_2:=(v,u)_1$, where $(\cdot,\cdot)_1$ is the first-variable-linear
Hilbert pairing of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]. Thus
$\langle u,v\rangle_2$ is linear in $v$ and conjugate-linear in $u$.
For each tensor product, use the same norm completion as
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], but equip it with the
second-variable-linear pairing obtained by conjugating that supplier's
first-variable-linear pairing. This leaves the norm and completion unchanged;
on elementary tensors it gives the product of the second-variable pairings.
Let $H^{\widehat\otimes n}$ be the iterated Hilbert tensor completion, with
$H^{\widehat\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$; the tensor inner product is the product of
the factor pairings. For $n\ge1$, let
$P_{s,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi$ and
$P_{a,n}=n!^{-1}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$, using the
permutation action and the orthogonal projections of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Define
$H_s^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{s,n}$ and
$H_a^{(n)}=\operatorname{ran}P_{a,n}$, with
$H_s^{(0)}=H_a^{(0)}=\mathbb C$. These are the symmetric and antisymmetric
$n$-particle sectors.

The bosonic and fermionic Fock Hilbert spaces are the square-summable direct
sums
$\mathcal F_s(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_s^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$ and
$\mathcal F_a(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_a^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, with the componentwise inner product.
Their vacuum is $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$. The finite-particle subspace
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ consists of sequences with only finitely many nonzero
components.

For $n\ge0$, bosonic creation on sector $n$ is
$a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{s,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
bosonic annihilation is
$a_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, where
$C_h(v)=\langle h,v\rangle_2$ and its tensor extension is the bounded map of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], and $a(h)\Omega=0$. Define fermionic creation
by $c_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}P_{a,n+1}(h\otimes\Psi_n)$; for $n\ge1$,
fermionic annihilation is the corresponding first-factor contraction
$c_n(h)\Psi_n=\sqrt n(C_h\otimes I^{\otimes(n-1)})\Psi_n$, and
$c(h)\Omega=0$. The annihilation maps are conjugate-linear in $h$; the
creation maps are linear in $h$. These formulas define sector maps on the
finite-particle subspace; their maximal closed domains and operator relations are proved in
[[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. No physical statistics assignment or spin–statistics
theorem is part of these mathematical definitions.

derivations.claim: The integral in $g_j$ is the spacetime Fourier transform of a compactly supported smooth function, hence decreases faster than every inverse power of $|(\omega,\mathbf k)|$ by repeated integration by parts. Near $\mathbf k=0$, it is bounded by $\int|j|$, while the squared prefactor is $1/(2\omega)=1/(2|\mathbf k|)$. The radial integral of this bound is a constant times $\int_0^1r^2/r\,dr<\infty$. At infinity the rapid Fourier decay and $\|P_T\|\le1$ make the squared norm integrable. Also $P_Tg_j=g_j$ almost everywhere. Therefore $g_j\in\mathcal H_T$.

By [F3], a vector in $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ has only finitely many nonzero sectors. On each such sector [F2] bounds creation and annihilation by the corresponding square-root particle number times $\|g_j\|\|\Psi_n\|$. Thus both maps and their sum are defined on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. The same estimates bound every matrix element between fixed finite-particle vectors by a constant times $\|g_j\|$. On each fixed compact support, repeated integration by parts in step 1.1 bounds $\|g_j\|$ by finitely many smooth-test seminorms, so these matrix elements are continuous in the test-function topology. This proves the asserted distributional smearing without defining a point field.

Apply the CCR [F2] to the positive- and negative-frequency terms of the mode expansion and use $E=-\partial_0A$. At equal time the two cross terms combine to
$$-i\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3} \left(\delta_{ij}-\frac{k_i k_j}{|\mathbf k|^2}\right)e^{i\mathbf k\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf y)}.$$
This is the distributional Fourier multiplier $-iP_{T,ij}(-i\nabla_{\mathbf x})\delta^3(\mathbf x-\mathbf y)$; its action is defined by pairing the bounded multiplier against Schwartz tests. Thus the equal-time commutator holds after smearing, as claimed.

boundaries.reason: Statement of Smeared Coulomb photon operator distribution: Assume Countable Choice. Let $j=(j_1,j_2,j_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R^3)$ and use $\mathcal H_T$ and $P_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. For $\omega=|\mathbf k|$ and $\mathbf k\ne0$, define $$g_j(\mathbf k)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{3/2}(2\omega)^{1/2}}\, P_T(\mathbf k)\int_{\mathbb R^4}j(x)e^{i\omega x^0-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,d^4x.$$ Then $g_j\in\mathcal H_T$. On the finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ of the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$, the smeared transverse potential is $$A_T(j)=a(g_j)+a^\dagger(g_j).$$ Its matrix elements are continuous in the test-function topology; it is an operator-valued distribution and does not assign a pointwise operator to $A_i(x)$. The specified witness, fixed coordinate space or supplied Hilbert/test objects are the inputs of this assertion; it does not assert a separate existence result after replacing them by an empty underlying set.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 gives g_j=0 for the zero test, so the smeared field is zero.
